record.original_question: Let F be a foliation of degree d ≥ 2 with non-hyperbolic singularities. Describe the directed positive ddc-closed currents of F, and determine when F can admit diffuse positive closed currents directed by the foliation.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. Assume that F is a foliation of degree d ≥ 2 with non-hyperbolic singularities. Describe the ddc-closed positive currents, directed by the foliation. In which case diffuse positive closed currents directed by the foliation do exist ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation by Riemann surfaces on the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$ of degree $d \geq 2$, and assume that all singularities of $\mathcal{F}$ are non-hyperbolic (a singularity is hyperbolic if, after local linearization of the underlying vector field, the ratio of eigenvalues is non-real; non-hyperbolic means this ratio is real, possibly negative or rational).

A positive $(1,1)$-current $T$ on $\mathbb{P}^2$ is said to be directed by $\mathcal{F}$ if, on every flow box of $\mathcal{F}$, $T$ is given by a positive measure on the transversal integrated against the integration currents along the local plaques. The current $T$ is called $dd^c$-closed if $dd^c T = 0$, closed if $dT = 0$, and diffuse if it gives no mass to any single leaf or analytic curve.

(a) Describe the cone of all positive $dd^c$-closed currents directed by $\mathcal{F}$.

(b) Determine the precise conditions under which $\mathcal{F}$ admits a diffuse positive closed current directed by the foliation.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction. While the analogous problem for hyperbolic singularities has been resolved (showing local positive closed currents near hyperbolic singularities are supported on separatrices, with directed harmonic currents fully described in works by Nguyên and collaborators), the non-hyperbolic case remains substantially open. Partial results exist for linearizable non-hyperbolic singularities (Nguyên, Ergodic Theory Dynam. Systems) and unique ergodicity has been established under additional invariant-curve hypotheses, but a full description of $dd^c$-closed directed currents and a complete classification of when diffuse closed directed currents exist for arbitrary foliations of degree $d\ge 2$ with non-hyperbolic singularities does not appear in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Directed harmonic currents near non-hyperbolic linearizable singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Studies directed harmonic currents in the linearizable non-hyperbolic case, addressing a special subclass of the broader problem.
status_evidence.claim: Only the linearizable non-hyperbolic case has a published treatment, indicating partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Directed harmonic currents near hyperbolic singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves the analogous question in the hyperbolic case.
status_evidence.claim: The hyperbolic counterpart has been solved, leaving the non-hyperbolic problem as the natural open continuation.

status_evidence.title: Examples of harmonic foliated currents and singular Levi-flats on the projective plane
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) constructions of harmonic foliated currents on P^2.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research continues to address aspects of directed currents on P^2 without giving a complete description in the non-hyperbolic case.
